# Decoding the 2000 Camry Remote Programming Sequence

When attempting to program a remote for a 2000 Toyota Camry CE, the most common point of failure is the initiation sequence itself. Many online tutorials suggest variations involving opening and closing doors in specific patterns, but these instructions often fail because they conflate different model years or trim levels. To successfully enter programming mode on this specific vehicle architecture, you must rely on the key-fob cycling method rather than door manipulation sequences.

The correct procedure requires using an existing working remote to trigger a state change in the Body Control Module (BCM). First, ensure all doors are closed and the ignition is off. Press and hold the "Lock" button on your operational remote until the power windows cycle up and down automatically. This window cycling indicates that the BCM has successfully entered the high-security programming mode. At this exact moment, you must immediately press and release the "Unlock" button once within one to two seconds. If performed correctly, the door locks will cycle—typically locking once and unlocking once—to confirm the system is now listening for new transponder codes.

Once in this state, pressing any button on your new or blank remote should lock the doors again. You can program multiple remotes by repeating the "Lock" hold sequence followed by an "Unlock" press for each unit you wish to add. The process ends automatically after three minutes if no buttons are pressed, or immediately when the ignition is turned on. It is crucial to note that this method does not require a chip key; it relies entirely on RF signal detection from the fob itself.

A frequent misconception involves the distinction between valet keys and standard remote fobs. If your current key can open the glove box, you are likely dealing with a master key or a full-access key, but the physical ability to open compartments does not guarantee the presence of an active RF transmitter in the vehicle's memory. However, if the original factory remotes were lost years ago and never reprogrammed, the BCM may still retain slots for them, provided they haven't been manually erased via a diagnostic scan tool or by reaching the maximum capacity (usually four to five units).

If you attempt door-based sequences on this model year without success, it is often because those protocols apply to later generations of the Camry where immobilizer chips became mandatory. The 2000 CE variant predates widespread mandatory transponder requirements for non-chip keys in many regions, meaning the system relies heavily on the RF handshake described above.

There are no software commands or external diagnostic modes accessible via the OBD-II port that allow a user to manually force this state without physical interaction with the remotes. If you have exhausted all working remotes and cannot access the programming window, the only viable solution is dealer intervention using an IDS (Integrated Diagnostic System) scanner capable of bypassing the RF lockout or cloning existing signatures.
